first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction can improve early adoption. A small guarded test is preferable to competing on price, with qualified-revenue and lead-quality guardrails to detect downstream value loss.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, segmented onboarding-shortening experiment focused on self-serve accounts. The verified result directly addresses both declining onboarding completion and activation, with a substantial completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. Use signup-field reduction only where appropriate for SMBs, while monitoring qualified revenue and retention because its prior retention result was slightly negative and did not generalize beyond SMBs. Do not lead with promotional pricing, which may acquire lower-value accounts despite short-term volume.

final2.rationale: Respond with a tightly targeted, time-limited offer for price-sensitive SMB prospects and at-risk accounts rather than matching the competitor broadly. Prior evidence supports promotional pricing for this segment, but guard against subsidizing low-value demand and margin erosion by measuring qualified revenue, retention, expansion, and post-promotion churn. This urgent test should take priority over the onboarding experiment because SMB price-driven churn has doubled this week.
